syllabusTopics: Logic and set: statements, logical connectives, truth tables, theorems based on set operations
Real numbers: geometric representation of real numbers, interval, absolute value
Function: domain and range of a function, inverse function, composite function; algebraic (linear, quadratic and cubic) and transcendental (trigonometric, exponential, logarithmic) functions

Curve sketching: odd and even functions, periodicity, symmetry (about origin, X- and Y-axis), monotonicity; graphs of quadratic, cubic and rational functions, trigonometric (asinbx and acosbx), exponential (e^x), logarithmic (lnx)
Sequence and series: arithmetic, geometric, harmonic sequences and series and their properties; A.M, G.M, H.M and their relations; sum of infinite geometric series
Matrices and determinants: transpose of a matrix and its properties; minors and cofactors, adjoint, inverse matrix, determinant, properties of determinants (without proof)
Quadratic equation: nature and roots of a quadratic equation, relation between roots and coefficient, formation of a quadratic equation, symmetric roots, one or both roots common
Complex number: imaginary unit, algebra of complex numbers, geometric representation, absolute (modulus) value and conjugate of complex numbers and their properties, square root of a complex number

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - Σi = n(n+1)/2; Σi² = n(n+1)(2n+1)/6; Σi³ = [n(n+1)/2]² - Σₖ₌₁ⁿ (bₖ − bₖ₊₁) = b₁ − bₙ₊₁; sum to ∞: b₁ − lim bₙ - Σₖ₌₁ⁿ kxᵏ⁻¹ = (1 − xⁿ)/(1−x)² − nxⁿ/(1−x) → 1/(1−x)² for |x| < 1

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The collapsing spyglass*** - in sum 1/k - 1/(k+1) every interior term cancels its neighbour; only 1 and 1/(n+1) survive, and the limit finishes the job.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Series With Structure Beyond AP/GP lie the **special sums** (Σi, Σi², Σi³), **telescoping series**, and **arithmetico-geometric series**. Each carries a theorem-grade derivation — induction, telescoping collapse, or the shift trick — and each is a standard NEB computation.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 The special sums (theorems with proofs) - **Σᵢ₌₁ⁿ i = n(n+1)/2** — Gauss pairing: S forwards + S backwards = n columns of (n+1). - **Σi² = n(n+1)(2n+1)/6** — telescoping via (k+1)³ − k³ = 3k² + 3k + 1 summed over k. - **Σi³ = [n(n+1)/2]²** — same telescoping with (k² − (k−1)²)² or induction; the cube sum is the **square of the triangular sum**.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: n(n+1) sums: split into k^2 + k. 1/(k(k+1)): partial fractions then telescope. n x^(n-1): shift trick. Always end telescoping answers with the limit.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB-style (3m): Find the sum of the series 1·2 + 2·3 + 3·4 + ⋯ + n(n+1).** — **Split by linearity:** k(k+1) = k² + k, so Sₙ = Σk² + Σk. **Apply the special sums:** Σk² = n(n+1)(2n+1)/6 and Σk = n(n+1)/2. **Combine:** Sₙ = n(n+1)(2n+1)/6 + n(n+1)/2 = n(n+1)[(2n+1) + 3]/6 = **n(n+1)(n+2)/3**.…  ·  **NEB-style (3m): Find the sum to infinity of the series 1/(1·2) + 1/(2·3) + 1/(3·4) + ⋯** — **Step 1 — partial fractions:** 1/(k(k+1)) = 1/k − 1/(k+1) (check: (k+1) − k = 1 over k(k+1) ✓). **Step 2 — telescoping partial sum:** Sₙ = (1 − ½) + (½ − ⅓) + (⅓ − ¼) + ⋯ + (1/n − 1/(n+1)).…

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Telescoping is cancellation engineering: partial fractions build the collapse, and the limit of the surviving tail decides convergence.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Special sums: sum i = n(n+1)/2 (Gauss pairing); sum i^2 = n(n+1)(2n+1)/6 and sum i^3 = [n(n+1)/2]^2 (telescoping via (k+1)^3 - k^3 = 3k^2 + 3k + 1, or induction). Telescoping: sum (b_k - b_{k+1}) = b_1 - lim b_{n+1}; converges iff the tail converges; partial fractions manufacture telescopes (1/(k(k+1)) = 1/k -…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Compound-interest schedules and depreciation tables are arithmetico-geometric sums - the shift trick is their accountant.
